summary: Extend the existing frontend-only Korean Team Builder app rather than rebuilding it. The current baseline already supports Excel paste input, validation, preview, and one best-team result. This iteration adds six ranked candidate combinations, optional header-row parsing, stronger role-group balance ranking with explicit tank priority, and a selectable candidate-detail UI. Existing unresolved real-browser/mobile QA remains documented but is not a blocker for this round.

milestones.title: Input Contract Update
milestones.objective: Support both header and no-header paste formats without regressing the current validation and preview flow.
deliverables: Update `src/lib/parseClipboard.js` so the first non-empty row is treated as a header only when it matches the canonical Korean columns `유저 이름 / 탱커 티어 / 딜러 티어 / 힐러 티어`; otherwise treat it as player data.

Keep the existing 10-player, duplicate-name, empty-cell, and unsupported-tier validation rules, but make row-number reporting correct in both modes: header-present input should keep spreadsheet row numbers, and headerless input should start from row 1.
Leave the normalized player shape unchanged enough that the existing preview table and optimizer can still consume it with minimal refactor.
Update Korean UI copy in `src/constants/copy.js` and the input help text in `src/lib/render.js` to state clearly that the header row is optional.
Add parser tests covering: valid input with header, valid input without header, malformed pseudo-header rows, and validation errors in both modes.

milestones.title: Candidate Ranking Engine
milestones.objective: Refactor the optimizer so it produces six distinct ranked candidate team splits using the new tie-break rules while preserving the current single-best recommendation behavior.
deliverables: Extend `src/lib/optimizer.js` to compute a richer candidate object for each distinct team split: both teams, total score difference, per-role team totals, role-score-difference sum, tank-score difference, unranked difference, and a canonical dedupe key.
Define `role-score-difference sum` as `abs(tank diff) + abs(damage diff) + abs(support diff)` using the assigned-role scores in the final candidate.
Deduplicate equivalent team pairings before ranking so the top six are six distinct candidate combinations, not repeated copies caused by enumeration order.

Implement ranking in this exact order: `1) total score difference asc`, `2) role-score-difference sum asc`, `3) tank-score difference asc`, `4) unranked difference asc`, `5) random order only inside groups that are identical on the first four metrics`.

Keep the old best-result flow by exposing a helper such as `getTopCandidates(players, { limit, rng })` and making `optimizeTeams(players)` return the first ranked candidate plus metadata for backward compatibility.
Inject the random function instead of calling `Math.random` directly inside ranking logic so tests can force deterministic order for full ties.

milestones.title: Candidate Selection UI
milestones.objective: Show six candidate summaries and let the user inspect one candidate in detail without making the UX complicated.
deliverables: Update app state in `src/main.js` and `src/lib/appFlow.js` to store `candidates`, `selectedCandidateId`, and the currently selected detail result; compute candidates once on `팀 나누기` and default-select the first ranked candidate.

Update `src/lib/render.js` to add a compact Korean candidate list section with six clickable cards or buttons labeled clearly, for example `후보 1` to `후보 6`, with the first candidate visually marked as the recommended default.
Each candidate summary must show at minimum: team A total, team B total, total score difference, role-score-difference sum, tank-score difference, and unranked difference.

Keep the existing detailed team board concept, but make it render the currently selected candidate so the user can inspect `팀 A / 팀 B`, assigned roles, tier labels, scores, and totals for the chosen option.
Clicking a candidate must update only the selected detail view and selected styling immediately, without clearing the pasted input or rerunning validation.
Adjust `src/styles.css` so the added candidate list remains readable on desktop and narrow widths, but do not spend the round on new browser-qa-only work beyond keeping the layout sane.

milestones.title: Verification And Handoff
milestones.objective: Lock the new behavior with automated checks and update project docs so the next agent or reviewer can verify the feature quickly.
deliverables: Expand `test/optimizer.test.js` with fixtures that prove ordering by total score difference, then role-score-difference sum, then tank-score difference, then unranked difference.
Add a full-tie optimizer test that injects a fake RNG and verifies randomization happens only within an exact-tie metric bucket.
Expand `test/appFlow.test.js` so the DOM flow asserts six candidates render, the first one is selected by default, and clicking another candidate updates the detailed team output immediately.
Keep `npm test` and `npm run build` as mandatory checks for this round; treat `npm run test:browser` as optional evidence only when a Chromium-family browser is available.
Update `README.md` with the optional-header input rule, six-candidate ranking logic, and the user flow for selecting a candidate.

Update `FINAL_OUTPUT.md` with implemented scope, explicit assumptions, exact verification commands run, and a note that unresolved real-browser/mobile evidence is still non-blocking in this iteration.

acceptance_criteria: Given the same valid 10-player roster, pasting it with the canonical header row or without any header row both succeed and produce candidate results instead of validation errors.
After clicking `팀 나누기` on a valid 10-player roster, exactly 6 distinct candidate combinations are shown.
Every candidate combination contains exactly 2 teams of 5 players, each team has `1탱 2딜 2힐`, and no player appears more than once within the candidate.
Each candidate summary shows team A and team B totals, absolute total score difference, role-score-difference sum, tank-score difference, and unranked difference in Korean UI.
Candidate ordering follows the required priority: total score difference first, then role-score-difference sum, then tank-score difference, then unranked difference.
When multiple candidates are identical on all four ranking metrics, only that tied group is randomized; with an injected test RNG, the order is reproducible.
The first ranked candidate is selected by default and displayed in the detailed team board, preserving the existing single-best recommendation flow.
When the user clicks another candidate, the detailed `팀 A / 팀 B` composition updates immediately without page reload and without clearing the pasted input.
Headerless invalid input and header-based invalid input both still return clear Korean validation messages for wrong player count, duplicate names, empty cells, and unsupported tiers.
`README.md` and `FINAL_OUTPUT.md` describe the new six-candidate feature, the optional-header rule, and the actual verification scope for this iteration.
test_strategy: Unit-test `parseClipboard` with four fixtures: valid with header, valid without header, malformed first row that should be treated as player data, and invalid data in both modes.

Unit-test optimizer ranking with purpose-built fixtures where only one tie-break level changes at a time: total score difference, then role-score-difference sum, then tank-score difference, then unranked difference.
Add a dedupe test that confirms the top six candidates are unique by canonical team-pair key.
Add a full-tie test that passes a stub RNG into the candidate-ranking function so exact-tie ordering can be asserted without flaky tests.
Extend the DOM app-flow test to cover candidate list rendering, default selection, candidate switching, and preserved input text after selection changes.
Run `npm test` and `npm run build` before handoff; run `npm run test:browser` only if a Chromium-family browser is present, and record clearly whether it was executed or skipped.

risks.risk: The optimizer may produce duplicate candidate rows because multiple enumeration paths can map to the same final team pairing.
risks.mitigation: Canonicalize team order, generate a stable dedupe key per pairing, store candidates in a `Map`, and test that the returned top six have unique keys.

risks.risk: Random tie-breaking can make automated tests flaky and can accidentally disturb non-tied ranking order.
risks.mitigation: Sort deterministically on the first four metrics, randomize only inside exact-tie buckets, and inject the RNG function so tests can use a fixed stub.

risks.risk: Optional header detection can misclassify the first player row as a header and silently drop a player.
risks.mitigation: Use strict header detection against the exact canonical Korean column names and add regression tests for headerless input whose first row contains normal player data.

risks.risk: Adding six candidates can make the result UI crowded and harder to scan than the current single-result board.
risks.mitigation: Keep summaries compact, show detailed rosters for only the selected candidate, and default-select the first recommendation instead of rendering six full boards at once.

risks.risk: Refactoring the optimizer for candidates can break the existing single-best result behavior that current tests and UI rely on.
risks.mitigation: Preserve a backward-compatible `optimizeTeams` entrypoint backed by the new ranked-candidate function and keep existing best-result assertions in the test suite.

risks.risk: The unresolved browser/mobile QA items from earlier rounds could distract implementation time away from the higher-priority candidate feature.
risks.mitigation: Treat real-browser verification as non-blocking this round, keep automated DOM/build coverage current, and document the remaining browser evidence gap honestly in handoff docs.

definition_of_done: The existing paste, validation, preview, and single-best-result workflow still works, with the first ranked candidate acting as the default recommendation.
The app accepts both header-present and headerless Excel-style paste input.
The app produces 6 distinct candidate combinations ranked by total score difference, role-score-difference sum, tank-score difference, and unranked difference, with randomization only for full ties.
The user can click any candidate and immediately inspect its detailed team composition in Korean.
Automated tests cover parser mode detection, optimizer ranking, candidate uniqueness, and candidate-selection UI behavior.
`npm test` and `npm run build` pass for the final workspace state.
`README.md` and `FINAL_OUTPUT.md` are updated to match the implemented feature set and this round's actual verification scope.
open_questions: Assumption: `role-score-difference sum` means the sum of absolute assigned-role score gaps for `tank`, `damage`, and `support` across the two teams.
Assumption: `언랭 분배 차이` means the absolute difference in total unranked assigned-role counts between the two teams, not role-specific unranked balancing.
Assumption: `후보 조합 6개` means 6 distinct final team pairings after canonical deduplication; duplicate partitions from enumeration should not be shown separately.
Assumption: optional header support only auto-detects the canonical Korean header row; any other first row is treated as player data and validated normally.

Assumption: real-browser/mobile verification from previous QA remains documented but is intentionally non-blocking for this feature-focused round unless a browser is available to run `npm run test:browser`.
